solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pretty mates who break up

indicators.note: when things break up their pieces scatter, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Attractive friends who split from each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty used as an adverb, as in 'pretty tired', means to some degree, a synonym.

clue.text: Minister not getting on in the Home Counties is by no means dense

indicators.note: the shortened minister goes inside the region's letters

parts.note: SE, south-east England, where the Home Counties surrounding London lie

indicators.note: the minister word does without the two letters of 'on'

parts.note: a parson is a church minister

explanation.surface: A clergyman out of favour in the commuter belt is anything but stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, all in the south-east of England; 'dense' looks like stupidity but here means thick.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly scattered is the opposite of thick or crowded, so it is far from packed.

clue.text: Low fellow once regarded as antisocial is put forward

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth seen as a troublemaker

explanation.surface: A disreputable fellow is proposed for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits, viewed as yobs.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea that is mooted has been raised for discussion, a synonym.

clue.text: Where bait is put out for wild animal

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about where to leave bait for a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar bear of the Arctic is also known by this colour-based name.

clue.text: Being disputatious — over a matter to be settled before the cricket match?

definitions.meaning: quarrelling over something already settled or trivial

definitions.text: over a matter to be settled before the cricket match?
definitions.meaning: a coin flip decides which side bats first, so one could dispute it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pointlessly disputing a decided matter; literally, quarrelling about the coin flip before play.

clue.text: That female's getting hold of me, someone bringing message

indicators.note: one piece grips the other, so the word for me sits inside the possessive for that female

parts.note: the possessive of 'she' is hers

explanation.surface: A woman grabs the speaker, who turns out to be a courier with a message.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the god Hermes was herald and messenger of the Olympians.

clue.text: Female bishop leaving the site where Jacob had dream

indicators.note: the bishop departs, so his letter is taken out of the place name

parts.words: the site where Jacob had dream
parts.note: Bethel, where Jacob dreamt of a ladder to heaven in Genesis
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A woman bishop quits the place of Jacob's ladder vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for any woman, a typical crossword use.

clue.text: Is America restricted by old trickster? There's cruel treatment

indicators.note: the first pieces are hemmed in by the trickster word around them

parts.note: mage is an archaic word for a magician
US, the United States

explanation.surface: An old con man controls America, a cause for ill-treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Misusage means bad or harsh handling, the same as abuse; a synonym.

clue.text: Extravagant folk, poet Stephen's family?

definitions.meaning: people who splash out money freely
the relatives of the English poet Stephen Spender, read as a plural surname

explanation.definitionFit: Big spenders are lavish people; the plural surname also suggests the household of poet Stephen Spender.

clue.text: Bar in hotel then is fantastic — poet's even seen in it

indicators.note: the poetic word appears within the rearranged letters
fantastic suggests the three words are made into something fanciful, so they are rearranged

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A hotel bar is superb, and a poet is spotted there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is fantastic' rearranges IN HOTEL THEN to NINETTHHOLE, and 'seen in it' places the poetic contraction inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers jokingly call the clubhouse bar the hole after the eighteenth, where the round really ends.

clue.text: Loving a party group

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a ring is a group or gang, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: A party crowd of affectionate people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe showing deep affection; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Hurriedly getting home — has left office finally

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the words left and office

explanation.surface: Someone rushes home after leaving work at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something in a hurry is to do it hastily, an idiom.

clue.text: Screen is put back with temptress behind it

indicators.note: behind places the temptress after the reversed pair of letters
putting the word back turns it round so it reads from right to left

parts.note: Eve tempted Adam with the apple in Genesis

explanation.surface: A screen is moved back with a seductress lurking behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen is to sift or filter out, as with a mesh utensil; a synonym.

clue.text: One bargain is obtained by newspaper person — perfect!

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a deal is a bargain or agreement
ED is short for editor, a person running a newspaper

explanation.surface: A journalist secures a bargain and declares it perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something idealised has been made to seem flawless, so it is presented as perfect.

clue.text: Fast food very English — eggier grub, looking nasty

indicators.note: grub that looks nasty is mangled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A very English takeaway of unappetising, overly eggy grub.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatless patty in a bun is a familiar item of quick takeaway food.

clue.text: A Parisian female, no good, old, with no prospect of marriage

parts.note: une is the French feminine form of 'a'
aged means old

explanation.surface: An elderly, useless Frenchwoman with no hope of a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not betrothed has no wedding planned, so no prospect of marriage.

clue.text: Red wine, very good, not mature

parts.note: pi is crossword shorthand for pious, very good
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A red wine described as excellent but not yet ready to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinotage is a South African red grape and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Exquisite eastern article, not fake

parts.note: the is the definite article
real means genuine, not fake

explanation.surface: An oriental object of great beauty that is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicately light and refined, close to exquisite in sense.

clue.text: Switches in strange niche awkwardly placed

indicators.note: the letters are placed awkwardly, that is, in a new jumbled order

explanation.surface: Light switches have been fitted in an odd recess.
explanation.definitionFit: Switches as a noun means swaps or exchanges, a synonym.

clue.text: Someone eating has a double portion of something in meal

indicators.note: the eater holds an extra letter within

parts.note: a diner is a person eating a meal
n stands for an unspecified number, a something; adding it beside the existing one doubles it

explanation.surface: A diner gets twice the helping of something in the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The eater word already has one N; putting in a second gives the double portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: It's fine to change last bit of clue

parts.note: to amend is to change or revise

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A setter is happy to alter the end of a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An amende is a monetary penalty or reparation, a French-derived word for a fine.

clue.text: Be stronger than sweetheart losing head before wedding

indicators.note: before puts the shortened sweetheart ahead of the wedding word
the sweetheart word loses its first letter

parts.note: a lover is a sweetheart
a match is a marriage, as in 'a good match'

explanation.surface: A suitor faces a setback just ahead of the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes the L off LOVER, leaving OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To overmatch an opponent is to be superior to them in strength or skill.

clue.text: Unhappy I am, upset — the magic touch works badly for me!

definitions.text: the magic touch works badly for me!

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: sad means unhappy
I'm is short for I am

explanation.surface: A miserable speaker laments that their golden touch is a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset turns SADIM over into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: King Midas wished that all he touched became gold, and then could not eat.

clue.text: One of two story-tellers, awful to listen to

indicators.note: how the word sounds when heard, not how it is written

parts.note: grim means dreadful or awful

explanation.surface: One of a pair of storytellers is painful to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brothers Grimm, Jacob and Wilhelm, collected German fairy tales; either is one of the pair.

clue.text: Information in notice, as supplied in lists

indicators.note: the information word goes in the middle of the notice word

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Details in a notice, supplied as lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Agendas are lists of items to be dealt with at meetings.

clue.text: System of rules broken in Rangoon

indicators.note: the city name is broken apart and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Regulations being flouted in the Burmese capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An organon is a body of principles or method of reasoning, after Aristotle's logical works.

clue.text: Recruit from Aberdeen, listening

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A new soldier signs up from Aberdeen while listening in.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit, as a verb, is to sign people up for the forces; a synonym.

clue.text: What church thief may obtain as a type of fuel

definitions.meaning: thieves strip roofing metal from churches and so get it for nothing
petrol made without the additive tetraethyl

explanation.definitionFit: Unleaded petrol is sold under this label; split in two, the words describe stolen roofing metal.
